chunks: Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man travelling on one of the roads of the Muslims on his riding animal, and it strikes with its leg, so he said:

He is not liable for what it strikes with its leg, but he is liable for what it strikes with its foreleg. If it is standing still, then he is liable for what it strikes with its foreleg and its leg. And if he is driving it, then he is liable also for what it strikes with its foreleg and its leg.

key_terms.أَصَابَتْ: it struck, hit, or caused harm
key_terms.بِرِجْلِهَا: with its hind leg or leg, referring to a type of strike or kick
key_terms.بِيَدِهَا: with its foreleg, referring to a forward strike by the animal
key_terms.دَابَّتِهِ: his riding animal or beast being ridden
key_terms.وَقَفَتْ: when it stood still or stopped
key_terms.يَسُوقُهَا: he was driving or leading it onward

ai.seo_question: When is a person liable for damage caused by his animal on a public road according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling regarding liability for damage caused by a riding animal on a public road. It distinguishes between cases based on the rider’s degree of control over the animal, making liability depend on whether the harm resulted from conduct attributed to the rider’s handling or restraint of the animal.
